transcript.speaker: Sam
transcript.text: What is the salary range?

transcript.speaker: Leah
transcript.text: For this level it is one hundred and twenty to one hundred and forty thousand.

transcript.speaker: Sam
transcript.text: Could you share the compensation band?

transcript.speaker: Leah
transcript.text: I'd rather not share numbers until after the technical round.

transcript.speaker: Sam
transcript.text: And pay?

transcript.speaker: Leah
transcript.text: The base is ninety thousand. Sorry, I misread, it is ninety-five thousand base, plus a bonus.

transcript.speaker: Leah
transcript.text: Tell me about your background.

transcript.speaker: Sam
transcript.text: I have been a backend engineer for six years.

transcript.speaker: Leah
transcript.text: Great, the team works mostly in Go.

transcript.speaker: Sam
transcript.text: How big is the team?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Eight engineers, a designer and a product manager.

label.answer: 8 engineers plus a designer and a PM

transcript.speaker: Sam
transcript.text: Who would I work with day to day?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: You would pair a lot with Ana and Ben, and the three of you would be the whole backend team.

transcript.speaker: Sam
transcript.text: How many people are on the team?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Six. Well, five, since Chloe moved to platform last week.

transcript.speaker: Sam
transcript.text: What is the remote policy?

transcript.speaker: Leah
transcript.text: Hybrid: Tuesdays and Thursdays in the office, the rest from home.

aliases: Tuesdays and Thursdays in the office

transcript.speaker: Sam
transcript.text: Would I need to relocate?

transcript.speaker: Leah
transcript.text: No, the whole company is fully remote, we meet in person twice a year.

aliases: fully remote with two meetups a year

transcript.speaker: Sam
transcript.text: Can I work from home?

transcript.speaker: Leah
transcript.text: That's something the hiring manager decides per team, I don't want to promise anything.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: When could you start?

transcript.speaker: Sam
transcript.text: After my notice period.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: We were hoping for someone by the first of March.

transcript.speaker: Sam
transcript.text: When would the role start?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Ideally in January. Actually, scratch that, budget opens in February, so February.

transcript.speaker: Sam
transcript.text: What happens after today?

transcript.speaker: Leah
transcript.text: A technical interview with two engineers, then a chat with the director.

transcript.speaker: Leah
transcript.text: We'll send you a take-home exercise tomorrow, and if that goes well you'll meet the team on site.

label.answer: take-home exercise, then on-site with the team

transcript.speaker: Sam
transcript.text: What are the next steps?

transcript.speaker: Leah
transcript.text: We're still figuring out the process for this role, I'll email you.

transcript.speaker: Sam
transcript.text: What do you build with?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Go services, a TypeScript front end, Postgres, all on Kubernetes.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Last month we rewrote the billing service from Ruby to Kotlin, which is what everything new is in now.

transcript.speaker: Sam
transcript.text: Which languages?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Mostly Python. Oh, sorry, I was thinking of my last job. Here it is Rust and Elixir.

transcript.speaker: Sam
transcript.text: Is there on-call?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Yes, one week in six, with a paid allowance.

transcript.speaker: Sam
transcript.text: How does on-call work?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Good question, let us come back to that in the next round.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Nobody here carries a pager, the platform team handles incidents out of hours.

transcript.speaker: Sam
transcript.text: Do you sponsor visas?

transcript.speaker: Leah
transcript.text: Yes, we sponsor Skilled Worker visas and cover the fees.

transcript.speaker: Sam
transcript.text: Is sponsorship possible?

transcript.speaker: Leah
transcript.text: Unfortunately not for this role, candidates need existing right to work.

transcript.speaker: Sam
transcript.text: What about visas?

transcript.speaker: Leah
transcript.text: I need to check with legal and get back to you.

transcript.speaker: Sam
transcript.text: How big is the team?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Growing fast! We have big plans for next year.

transcript.speaker: Leah
transcript.text: Just so you know, the offer would be around a hundred and ten thousand, depending on the level we land on.

transcript.speaker: Sam
transcript.text: Remote?

transcript.speaker: Leah
transcript.text: Fully in office. Hmm, no, I tell a lie, it changed in September: three days in the office.

transcript.speaker: Sam
transcript.text: I like hiking at weekends.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Oh nice, where do you go?
